Article Title: Non fossil power capacity crosses 300GW mark
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India’s installed clean energy generation capacity has crossed the 300GW mark, taking the country past 60% of its target of having 500GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.According to data released by renewable energy ministry, total non-fossil capacity stood at 300.5GW as on July 31, accounting for over 54% of total installed power generation capacity of around 552GW. Solar accounts for the largest share at 164.6GW, followed by large and small hydro at 57.2GW and wind at 58.1GW. Bio-power contributes nearly 11.8GW, while nuclear energy accounts for 8.8GW.The ministry said that a record 55.3GW of non-fossil capacity was added in 2025-26, including 44.6GW of solar and 6GW of wind capacity. Solar-led capacity addition rose from 2.8GW in 2014 to nearly 165GW now, while wind capacity has increased from 21GW to over 58GW during the same period.The rise in renewable capacity has also pushed up clean power generation, which increased from about 191 billion units in 2014-15 to 477.8 billion units in 2025-26.The ministry said domestic manufacturing capacity for renewable energy equipment has also expanded, with the approved list of models and manufacturers for solar PV modules crossing 200GW, compared with 2.3GW in 2014, helped by the production-linked incentive scheme for high-efficiency solar modules.Govt is also implementing National Green Hydrogen Mission to build capacity for production and use of green hydrogen and its derivatives, with the aim of reducing emissions from hard-to-abate sectors and cutting dependence on imported fossil fuels.
Article Summary: Total non-fossil capacity stood at 300.5gw as on july 31. Solar accounts for the largest share at 164.6gw, followed by large and small hydro at 57.2gw and wind at 58.1gw. Bio-power contributes nearly 11.8gw, while nuclear energy accounts for 8.8 gw.

Article Title: Meta must comply with Indian law, not merely global policies: Centre
Article Text:
Meta must follow Indian law, not just global rules: Govt after MeitY talks (Mark Zuckerberg)

NEW DELHI: Meta's platforms must comply with Indian law and cannot be governed solely by the company's global policies, news agency ANI reported quoting government sources said on Sunday.This follows a series of meetings between the social media giant and the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY). Officials also clarified that it would be factually incorrect to say the government had "directed Meta to completely overhaul its algorithm".The government’s focus, is on ensuring that Meta’s content policies, platform guidelines and moderation systems are aligned with Indian law. While concerns remain, officials said the discussions are aimed at securing concrete changes from the company rather than simply seeking assurances, ANI reported quoting sources.Sources told ANI that India's cultural context is not always fully understood by teams based outside the country. They said Meta needs greater local input, including stronger understanding of Indian languages and cultural nuances, to improve content moderation in India.The latest clarification came after a meeting on Friday between Meta's technical team and MeitY officials, during which the company explained its existing systems for handling harmful content online. Technical discussions between the two sides remain underway, with another round of meetings expected next week, sources said.On child sexual abuse material (CSAM), government sources told ANI that there is zero tolerance and zero compromise.Officials said allowing such material to remain on Meta's platforms would amount to a serious violation of rules. They said the company needs to adopt stronger and more proactive measures, with concrete action expected instead of assurances.The issue was also raised during earlier meetings between Meta's global team and government officials, amid wider concerns over the company's content moderation systems.The government has also raised concerns over deepfakes involving prominent personalities.Sources told ANI that content posted from authorised or verified handles should not be incorrectly identified as deepfakes. Officials said such sensitive cases cannot be left entirely to automated detection systems and called for a "human-in-the-loop" mechanism to ensure content is properly reviewed before any takedown.The government has also questioned Meta over synthetically generated content that reappears after being identified and removed as a deepfake.Officials have sought details from Meta on the concrete steps it is taking to prevent such content from resurfacing after removal.Meta's recommendation and virality algorithms have also come under scrutiny during the discussions.The government questioned why users are frequently shown content unrelated to their stated interests and whether this points to shortcomings in Meta's recommendation systems, ANI reported.Officials also asked why synthetically generated content continues to be amplified through the company's algorithms.The government has insisted that once such content is flagged, it should not be recommended further or repeatedly resurface on the platform, sources said.The issue of Meta's recommendation systems had also figured in earlier meetings with IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and senior ministry officials, when the company's global team was questioned about its algorithms and compliance with Indian laws.The latest discussions follow several rounds of engagement between Meta and the Indian government over deepfakes, CSAM, bot accounts, synthetic content and the company's compliance with Indian laws.According to earlier reports, Meta's technical team had explained its proposed measures to address the concerns raised by the government and said it had solutions to tackle deepfakes, CSAM and bot accounts.The government has also been examining Meta's compliance with intermediary provisions under Indian law, including the conditions governing safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act.The Centre had earlier sought action against deepfake content and was examining whether Meta's role in determining what content users see could have implications for its status as an intermediary.The latest discussions, however, have focused on the technical functioning of Meta's systems and how its global policies are implemented in India.As the talks continue, government sources said the objective is not to demand a complete overhaul of Meta's algorithm but to ensure that its platforms, content policies and moderation mechanisms comply with Indian law and adequately account for India's linguistic and cultural context.
Article Summary: Meta must follow indian law, not just global rules: govt after meity talks. Meta needs greater local input, including stronger understanding of indian languages and cultural nuances, to improve content moderation in india. The government’s focus, is on ensuring that meta’'s content policies, platform guidelines and moderation systems are aligned with indian law.

Article Title: "He’s been abusing steroids since the age of 14": Clavicular faces explosive steroid controversy as Greg Doucette questions his natural physique claims
Article Text:
What Greg Doucette said about Clavicular and steroid allegations

Why the Clavicular steroid controversy is drawing attention

Clavicular has built a major online identity around looksmaxxing and physical appearance, but a fresh controversy is putting his claims under a harsh spotlight. A post circulating on X attributes a blunt critique to fitness personality Greg Doucette, who questioned whether Clavicular’s public image matches his alleged approach to performance and physique. The comments have quickly turned attention toward the growing debate over steroids, testosterone use and authenticity in online fitness culture.The controversy centers on remarks attributed to Greg Doucette in the post shared by Clavicular Updates. Doucette reportedly challenged the idea of Clavicular presenting himself as a natural figure within the looksmaxxing space.The post quotes him saying:“Clavicular, the face of looksmaxxing, isn’t looksmaxxing! Does any of this make sense? It’s like a financial advisor not having any money, not saving, wasting it all, or a marriage counselor who’s been through 5 divorces, How is that possible?”The criticism then became more pointed, with Doucette allegedly questioning claims about Clavicular’s reported use of performance-enhancing substances.“Apparently Clavicular is natural, because realistically he is, besides the fact he’s been abusing steroids since the age of 14, despite the fact he’s on 10 mg of Reta(trutide) right now... Does this look like a guy who is on high doses of HRT? A guy who has essentially lost all of his muscle... If Clavicular is on 200 mg of test a week and/or more, that is not TRT, that is a low dose (ster-id) cycle.”These are serious claims, and they should be treated as allegations rather than established facts.The image does not provide independent evidence proving that Clavicular used steroids from a particular age or that he is currently taking any specific substance or dosage.The dispute goes beyond one influencer or one viral post. Clavicular has become closely associated with the looksmaxxing movement, a broad online culture focused on improving physical appearance through grooming, fitness, style and other methods.That makes claims about his own physique especially sensitive. If an influencer promotes a particular approach to appearance while allegedly relying on methods that are not openly disclosed, audiences may question how much of the transformation is attainable naturally.Doucette’s comparison is built around that perceived contradiction. His central argument is not simply about appearance. It is about credibility.The controversy also highlights a bigger problem in online fitness spaces. Viewers often see dramatic physiques, rapid transformations and confident claims without knowing the full story behind them. Some creators openly discuss performance-enhancing drugs, while others deny using them. In many cases, audiences are left trying to separate documented information from speculation.For Clavicular, the latest criticism adds another layer to an already highly scrutinized online persona. The accusations circulating in the post may generate plenty of discussion, but they do not independently establish steroid use or prove the specific medical claims being made.That distinction matters. Viral fitness controversies can spread far faster than evidence.For now, the biggest takeaway is the challenge Doucette’s alleged comments have placed before Clavicular: whether the image presented online accurately reflects the methods behind his physique. Until verifiable evidence emerges, the steroid-related allegations remain claims rather than confirmed facts.
Article Summary: Clavicular has built a major online identity around looksmaxxing and physical appearance. A fresh controversy is putting his claims under a harsh spotlight. A post circulating on x attributes a blunt critique to fitness personality greg doucette. The comments have quickly turned attention toward the growing debate over steroids, testosterone use and authenticity.

Article Title: "It malfunctioned...": Kyle Shanahan blames Tesla after terrifying car crash as 49ers coach raises shocking Autopilot questions
Article Text:
Kyle Shanahan (Image via Getty)

What Kyle Shanahan revealed about the Tesla car crash

Could Kyle Shanahan’s crash create trouble for Tesla?

San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan is offering a deeper look at the July 11 car crash that left him with multiple injuries. Shanahan previously accepted responsibility after reaching for his phone while driving, but he now says he cannot rule out a possible issue involving his Tesla Model S and its Autopilot system. His comments add a new layer to an accident that already raised serious concerns.Shanahan initially said the crash happened after his phone slipped from his lap and he turned to retrieve it. His vehicle then moved into oncoming traffic, resulting in an accident that left the longtime 49ers coach injured.While speaking about the incident again this week, Shanahan explained that he still considers himself responsible. However, he also acknowledged that he is unsure what happened with the vehicle's driving system at the moment of impact.“I’ve had autopilot for nine years, so I’m pretty comfortable with it and, you know, who knows what happened when I turned around? Whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off? That’s something I don’t know yet. But regardless... it is always your fault, whether you’re on autopilot or not. You can’t take your eyes off the road. It’s a partnership driving, you don’t just turn it over to a computer, and it’s a good lesson, no matter how comfortable I am with that, that I believe someday could save my life or someone else’s”That admission is important because Shanahan did not definitively blame Tesla.Instead, he raised the possibility that the Autopilot system may have behaved unexpectedly or that he could have accidentally disengaged it while reaching for his phone.His comments also highlight a broader point about driver-assistance technology. Shanahan stressed that drivers remain responsible for paying attention, even when they have become comfortable using automated features.Shanahan’s latest comments have already added speculation about whether Tesla could face further questions over the accident. Some people have pointed to previous reports involving alleged problems with Autopilot, although Shanahan himself has not confirmed that a malfunction caused his crash.That distinction matters. At this stage, there is no established finding that Tesla’s technology caused the accident.The coach’s own account still places responsibility on the driver. His concern is that he cannot explain exactly what happened when he turned away from the road. Whether the system malfunctioned or he accidentally changed its operation remains unclear.For Shanahan, the incident also serves as a personal warning. The 49ers coach has acknowledged how dangerous even a brief distraction can become behind the wheel. His willingness to discuss the crash could also encourage other drivers to avoid becoming overly dependent on driver-assistance technology.The timing is especially notable for San Francisco. Shanahan is coming off a strong 2025 campaign in which the 49ers finished 12-5 and won a playoff game after struggling through a 6-11 season the year before.Now, with the 2026 season approaching, the focus will shift back to football. But the coach's recovery and the unanswered questions surrounding his Tesla crash will remain part of his offseason story.
Article Summary: San francisco 49ers head coach kyle shanahan is offering a deeper look at the july 11 car crash that left him with multiple injuries. Shanahan previously accepted responsibility after reaching for his phone while driving, but he now says he cannot rule out a possible issue involving his tesla model s and its autopilot system.

Article Title: Tokyo's geisha population fell from about 13,000 in 1940 to around 200 today; one 86-year-old geisha is turning to AI and holograms to keep the culture alive
Article Text:
Years of hospitality

Worrying for the future

In one of the busy malls in Tokyo, Ikuko, Japan's oldest and most famous geisha dances for shoppers in an elegant black kimono with precise movements. Only, the 86-year-old isn't really there; it's her hologram, a 3D projection of her, displayed in a life-size white box. "Thank you very much," she said to passers-by, before bowing and changing to a younger version of herself, created with AI.While she doesn't think AI is "cut out for this dance" just yet, or to replace their legendary hospitality, with the geisha numbers dwindling in the country, Ikuko has resigned to embracing new things in order to save the country's most iconic art forms.Once, there were 200 geisha in Akasaka, the area of Tokyo where Ikuko practises. But over the years, she has watched their number fall to about 20. "I felt we had to preserve this culture, so I did it for the sake of that very culture," she told ABC News. "This is the era we are entering, so I have to go along with it."After an illustrious career, which includes being the first geisha awarded Japan's prestigious Order of the Rising Sun, Ikuko feels the responsibility to preserve the tradition. "I'm already at the end of my life," she said."My greatest regret is that I hope Tokyo's geisha districts will truly survive for another few decades."A Geisha is a traditional Japanese female entertainer. Gei means art and sha means person, literally translating to "person of art." They are professional artists skilled in traditional Japanese music, dance, singing and conversation. They live and work in special districts called hanamachi or flower towns. There were once dozens of them in the city, but today only six major hanamachi remain, while the number of geisha across the city has also fallen from about 13,000 in 1940 to around 200.With their striking white makeup and bold black wigs, geisha have been synonymous with Japan for centuries, but a lot of people, even locals, fail to understand what they do. Geisha operate largely behind closed doors, traditionally catering to an exclusive group of customers. They are artisans who are said to embody omotenashi, the Japanese art of wholehearted, selfless hospitality.They dedicate their lives to perfecting traditional Japanese arts, which they rehearse by day. At night, they host banquets in exclusive, high-end restaurants and specialist teahouses, which have traditionally been run on a referral-only basis, where new patrons must have an introduction from an existing client. At a banquet, they dance, play music on traditional instruments like the shamisen and taiko drum, and ensure conversation flows between guests."This is the very pinnacle of hospitality," Ikuko said. "Indeed, perhaps only the most distinguished guests are permitted to enter." In her career, she has entertained politicians, business leaders and chairmen.But she has also been confronted with the misconception that geisha are prostitutes. Once, during a visit to America, she ended up in hospital and had to spend her convalescence educating the nurses, who mistakenly thought she was a sex worker. Though having sex with clients has never been the job of a geisha, the lines have blurred at times, and Ikuko doesn't shy away from that history."In the old days, there were certainly many geisha who sacrificed themselves for their families and their households," she said. "Nobody wants that sort of thing anymore. There are no sellers and no buyers."It was in 1964, when Ikuko made her debut as a geisha in Tokyo as the city was hosting the Olympics. In the "busy, old days," she said, "if a booking for this banquet was 30 minutes, I'd have to rush straight off to the next one."But soon things began going downhill for the geisha. Iwashita Hisafumi, who was working in a prominent geisha district at the time, also remembers those days. It was 1993, and in an effort to clean up politics and protect confidentiality, then-prime minister Hosokawa Morihiro announced politicians and businessmen should stop using the restaurants, called ryotei, for meetings."From the very next day, I saw for myself that the customers stopped coming," Mr Iwashita said. "That was when the decline began." Ryotei restaurants started closing, and many of the city's geisha districts ceased to exist.Now a writer and expert on geisha, he is concerned Tokyo's remaining ryotei have been too slow to find new customers and income sources to keep the tradition alive. "Ultimately, it is culture, but culture cannot flourish where money doesn't flow," he said.Evolving with the new nowAt this point, everyone is trying to adapt to the ever-changing world. Geisha are no longer relying on referral or invitation to attend, and are instead advertising heavily on social media and taking bookings online. The experience has been tailored for tourists, with the crowd made up of guests from Mexico, Australia, the United States, Singapore and Germany."I feel we have to take one step, then another, and keep moving forward," said Okami Chikage, who became an apprentice geisha at just 15 years old and after 35 years of practising, took on a new role as the owner of Asakusa Miyakadori. "To do that, I think it might sometimes mean stepping slightly outside the tradition rather than sticking to it rigidly."Three geisha performed for the guests at the banquet, dancing and playing the shamisen, before playing a traditional drinking game called konpira fune fune.Geisha can have children in some areas, and technically they can get married and continue to practise, but many choose to retire to have a family. It's a life of intense dedication, but there are still young women signing up for it. These days, some geisha houses recruit apprentices online or on social media. Young hopefuls attend meetings with the houses to try to get accepted, and then it can take them anywhere from six months to several years to graduate.Ikuko wants the profession and legacy to continue and is lobbying for all six of Tokyo's major districts to come together for a joint performance. She believes promotion is key to preserving the tradition, and worries too few Japanese people even know there are still geisha in Tokyo.But first, she needs to persuade the city's politicians. She's currently meeting with a member of parliament and wants the Tokyo Metropolitan Government to protect the geisha districts.If the city government could help secure a venue for a joint performance, she believes the event could "bring the geisha world back to life, just like in the old days." In the meantime, she and her geisha recently took to the stage at the outdoor festival in her local neighbourhood of Akasaka, where they were greeted with loud cheers.
Article Summary: A geisha is a traditional japanese female entertainer. They are professional artists skilled in traditional japanese music, dance, singing and conversation. The number of geisha in tokyo has fallen from 13,000 in 1940 to around 200. "from the very next day, i saw for myself that the customers stopped coming," mr iwashita said.

Article Title: H-1B, L-1 visa extensions get costlier from Sept 9: What changes and who pays
Article Text:
US to charge H-1B, L-1 extension fee from September 9.

Have at least 50 employees in the US

Have more than 50 per cent of their US workforce on H-1B or L-1 visas

Fee scope widened

Indian IT firms face higher costs

The US has expanded the scope of a visa fee that could significantly raise immigration costs for large employers, with the USD 4,000 charge for H-1B petitions and USD 4,500 fee for L-1 petitions now set to apply to certain visa extension filings from September 9.The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said the revised rule will cover employers that meet the following criteria:For employers meeting these conditions, the fee will now apply not only to initial H-1B and L-1 petitions and certain change-of-employer petitions, but also to qualifying extension-of-stay petitions for existing employees.Earlier, the 9-11 Response and Biometric Entry-Exit Fee generally applied to initial H-1B and L-1 petitions and certain cases involving a change of employer. Routine extension petitions filed by the same employer were generally exempt from this particular fee.DHS said the new interpretation corrects its earlier reading of the law and requires covered employers to pay the biometric fee for all qualifying extension-of-status petitions. Amended petitions that do not seek an extension of the worker's authorised stay will continue to be exempt.The fee itself has not increased. Employers will pay USD 4,000 for each qualifying H-1B petition and USD 4,500 for each L-1 filing.DHS estimates the expanded collections could generate about USD 157.3 million annually, while separate estimates cited in the rule put additional collections at USD 37.9 million in fiscal 2026 and USD 40 million in fiscal 2027.The revenue is used to support the US Customs and Border Protection's biometric entry-exit system, which uses technologies including facial comparison to track and verify foreign nationals entering and leaving the country.The change could have a disproportionate impact on major Indian IT services and consulting companies, which employ large numbers of Indian professionals in the US on H-1B and L-1 visas.For firms managing thousands of such workers, the fee could now become a recurring cost when eligible employees seek extensions with the same employerDHS data cited in the rule shows that about 27 per cent of H-1B filings by covered employers incurred the biometric fee between fiscal years 2018 and 2025.Under the expanded interpretation, the department estimates that around 75 per cent of their H-1B petitions would have been subject to the charge.The higher recurring cost could prompt companies to reassess the economics of retaining foreign workers in the US, particularly those facing multiple visa extensions.For Indian professionals, who form a large share of the US H-1B workforce and often face lengthy employment-based green card backlogs, the higher employer costs could influence decisions on retaining workers on long-term US assignments.
Article Summary: Us to charge h-1b, l-1 extension fee from september 9. Have at least 50 employees in the us. Have more than 50 per cent of their us workforce on h/l-1 visas.fee scope widened to include qualifying extension-of-stay petitions.

Article Title: Microsoft warns travellers of attacks on hotel Wi-Fi; says: Hackers can record your video, audio, steal passwords; how to know and protect yourself
Article Text:
Microsoft cuts 4800 job

How ‘CaptiveCrunch’ hacker attack works

Microsoft revealed that the attacks takes place in two primary ways:

How travelers can stay safe

Microsoft’s Threat Intelligence team has issued a warning to travelers following a series of sophisticated cyberattacks targeting guest Wi-Fi networks at hotels and hospitality venues worldwide. The internet hijacking campaign, dubbed ‘CaptiveCrunch’, has been active since at least May and is attributed to Storm-2945, a sub-cluster claimed to be of the Russian hacking group Midnight Blizzard (also known as APT29 or Cozy Bear).According to Microsoft, the hacker group is executing "widespread but targeted" traffic manipulation attacks through Public guest networks and captive portal screens – the web pages that appear when users attempt to log onto hotel Wi-Fi or those at public places like airports, tourists venues and more. "To date, Microsoft has identified widespread compromise of Wi-Fi networks at hospitality-related organizations and other networks serviced by captive portal equipment in several countries. ReliaQuest has identified this activity not only at hotels, but also conference centers and other shared venues, and assesses that the goal of this activity is to access the accounts of corporate travelers," said Microsoft in its report.The hackers compromise the underlying Wi-Fi infrastructure of hospitality venues, redirecting unsuspecting guests through fake portals and malicious pop-ups. Once connected, victims are tricked into downloading malicious files or entering sensitive credentials under the guise of routine security checks.Fake Browser Updates: Guests attempting to connect to hotel Wi-Fi may be presented with pop-ups prompting them to update their web browser or run network troubleshooting utilities. Some prompts mimic official Google security checks with warnings such as: "Our systems have detected unusual traffic from your computer network. Please complete the security check to access Google Search."Account Takeovers: In other instances, users are redirected to convincing fake login screens. Once credentials are submitted, the attackers gain access to the victim's Microsoft 365 accounts, granting them entry to private emails, OneDrive documents, and corporate networks.Once malware is installed on a target device, the hijackers gain broad control. Microsoft warned that Storm-2945 can capture keystrokes, record audio and video, take screenshots, steal browser cookies and stored passwords, and remotely operate the infected device.Microsoft listed a number of potential fake windows that may pop up upon logging into a compromised network, prompting users to download updates or patches. They include:* "winupdate": A Windows Update screen displaying the words "Working on updates… Don't turn off your computer"* "defender": A fake Windows Security virus scan* "directx": A "DirectX End-User Runtime Web Installer"* "vcredist": A Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable installer* "sysopt": A disk optimization utility* "netfix": A false Windows Network Diagnostics tool* "browser": A browser update prompt* "pdfview": A document viewer installerMicrosoft urges both individual travelers and corporate IT departments to exercise extreme caution on public networks, recommending the following protective measures:Use Cellular Hotspots: Avoid public or hotel Wi-Fi networks whenever possible; instead, rely on personal cellular hotspots or encrypted private connections.Ignore Unexpected Pop-Ups: Never download browser updates, security tools, network certificates, or software updates offered directly through hotel captive portals or unexpected browser pop-ups.Limit Data Sharing: Companies should review and restrict the sensitive information employees provide to hospitality providers when traveling or logging onto guest networks.
Article Summary: 'captivecrunch' is a series of sophisticated cyberattacks targeting guest wi-fi networks at hotels and hospitality venues worldwide. The internet hijacking campaign, dubbed ‘captive crunch’, has been active since at least may and is attributed to storm-2945.

Article Title: Meta joins OpenAI and Anthropic, says our AI model went 'wild', but adds: We are 'not really responsible as …
Article Text:
Meta becomes the third AI company to report such incidents

What Irregular said about Meta’s Muse Spark breach

Calls for transparency

Meta has confirmed that its Muse Spark model exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service during cybersecurity testing, marking the company’s first public disclosure of a rouge AI incident. According to a report by Business Insider, in a statement, Meta said that the breach occurred due to a misconfiguration by Irregular, an independent firm it uses for model evaluations. The error allowed the model to access the internet during testing. Meta added that it learned of the incident when Irregular notified the company and is now investigating, promising a full retrospective once details are finalised.Meta’s disclosure makes it the third major AI company to report such incidents in recent weeks. OpenAI admitted that two of its models escaped test environments and hacked into Hugging Face, later self-reporting two additional lapses. Anthropic revealed that its Claude models had gained unauthorised access to external systems during testing. Hugging Face itself confirmed a breach last month, while other firms have faced similar rogue agent behaviour.Irregular, the testing company involved, said the incident was not a sophisticated cyberattack but rather an evaluation environment issue similar to Anthropic’s disclosure. “This did not involve a sandbox escape or a sophisticated cyber action. There are no current open issues,” a spokesperson said, adding that Irregular is preparing a white paper on best practices for containment and secure evaluations.The string of incidents has prompted calls for stronger AI safety regulation and mandatory disclosures. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue told CBS that transparency is critical, urging companies to share “agent traces” to determine whether lapses stemmed from human error, system flaws, or AI behavior. Industry leaders like Box CEO Aaron Levie have warned these breaches highlight the “wild times” ahead, as AI agents demonstrate the ability to escape systems, discover vulnerabilities, and hack external platforms.
Article Summary: Meta becomes the third ai company to report such incidents in recent weeks. Breach occurred due to a misconfiguration by irregular, an independent firm it uses for model evaluations. The error allowed the model to access the internet during testing. Meta added that it learned of the incident when irregular notified the company and is now investigating.

Article Title: As companies in America face rising health costs, Starbucks ends employee benefits' coverage for these medicines
Article Text:
Reason behind Starbucks pulling back coverage for weight-loss drugs

Starbucks discontinued its AI inventory tool

Starbucks has announced that it will stop covering the GLP-1 medications prescribed for weight loss under its employee health plans starting October. According to a report by Business Insider, the Seattle-based coffee chain has confirmed that while the drugs may still be covered for other conditions such as diabetes, they will no longer be included for weight-loss purposes. Starbucks provides health benefits to full- and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week.This move by Starbucks reflects a broader trend among US employers recalibrating benefits as spending on GLP-1 drugs surges. Originally developed for diabetes, these medicines have become popular for obesity treatment. According to the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans, GLP-1 drugs accounted for 11.4% of corporate employers’ total annual claims in 2025, up from 6.9% in 2023. Average health-benefit costs per employee rose 6% last year and are projected to climb another 6.7% this year, with GLP-1 usage cited as a major driver.Other large employers have also pulled back coverage. As per the Business Insider report, Allina Health ended GLP-1 coverage for weight loss in January 2025, citing rising premiums, while PwC has reportedly made similar changes. At the same time, some companies are doubling down: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan recently said the bank spends more than $250 million annually on GLP-1 coverage, viewing it as an investment in employee health.In related news, in May this year, Starbucks announced that it is discontinuing its AI-powered inventory management tool. As reported by Fortune, the company decided to stop using the system after employees raised concerns about its accuracy. The tool, developed by NomadGo, was introduced in September last year to automatically count inventory items such as milk and syrups and help stores manage stock levels. However, workers said the app often made mistakes, leading to operational problems. According to Carl Addison, a Starbucks shift supervisor in Washington state, the system required stores to reorganise storage areas, adding extra work for employees. “The app’s inaccuracies made employees’ workflow more challenging,” Addison told Fortune.

Article Title: Scientists turn Sharks into real-time ocean observers, carrying sensors that can measure conditions for oceanographic, atmospheric and climate models
Article Text:
AI generated image

Researchers decode ocean heat that fuels hurricanes

Tagging executed like a ‘Pit Crew’

Researchers from University of Delaware are transforming how oceanographers (scientists who study the earth's oceans) track marine conditions by deploying specialised electronic tags that turn living sharks into mobile, real-time data collection hubs. The research project, led by marine scientist Aaron Carlisle, equips predatory fish with advanced sensors designed to collect water profiles across the US East Coast.Instead of merely tracking animal movements, the tags gather critical data on temperature, salinity and depth – feeding real-time information directly into atmospheric and climate forecast models. The research was published in journal Frontiers in Conservation Science.The primary goal of the tagging initiative is to map the upper layer of the ocean, known to oceanographers as the mixed layer. This upper column of water holds the thermal energy that directly feeds and amplifies hurricane strength.“This is the part of the water column that really drives hurricane intensity — warmer mixed layer equals stronger hurricane — as it holds the heat that feeds hurricanes,” explained Carlisle, a professor in the university's School of Marine Science and Policy.While oceanographers have deployed sensor tags on marine mammals like elephant seals in polar regions, sharks present a unique advantage for Atlantic storm tracking. They are abundant, widely distributed, and traverse key coastal corridors where major hurricanes develop and gain strength before making landfall.Researchers target migratory species that surface frequently, such as shortfin mako sharks, blue sharks, smooth hammerheads and juvenile great white sharks. Frequent surfacing is critical because the electronic tags must reach the water's surface to transmit cached environmental data up to orbiting satellite networks.The research team conducts offshore expeditions aboard the university’s research vessel, deploying baited lines 30 to 60 kilometres off the Atlantic coast. When a shark is brought alongside the vessel, the team executes the tagging protocol with extreme precision under strict animal welfare guidelines.“The tagging process itself is operated like a pit crew in an auto race,” Carlisle said, emphasising that the procedure typically takes under five minutes. Each animal undergoes a quick health check before being tagged on its dorsal fin. To protect the sharks long-term, the tags are secured using metallic components designed to naturally corrode and shed after a predetermined period.
Article Summary: Researchers from university of delaware are transforming how oceanographers track marine conditions by deploying specialised electronic tags that turn living sharks into mobile, real-time data collection hubs. The research project, led by marine scientist aaron carlisle, equips predatory fish with advanced sensors designed to collect water profiles across the us east coast.

Article Title: Google Drive is ending Google Photos backup starting August 10: What settings users need to change before deadline to ensure not losing photos and videos
Article Text:
What is changing for Google Photos users

What to do to keep your Google Photos back up

Google has confirmed that its Drive desktop app will stop supporting automatic Google Photos backup starting August 10, 2026. The change means that the users who rely on Drive’s desktop client to sync photos and videos from their computers will no longer see a new media automatically backed up to Google Photos. The company said that this move is part of its effort to simplify backup tools and also focus on dedicated photo management via the Photos app. “Google Drive for desktop ends support for Google Photos backup on August 10, 2026. To stop backing up existing folders before this date, use these instructions. To continue backing up folders after this date, you must add photos & videos from Google Drive to Google Photos,” said Google.Currently, the Google Drive desktop app allows users to designate a folder on their computer to be automatically backed up to Google Photos, a convenient way to keep photo libraries synced to the cloud without manual uploads. From August 10, that automatic connection between Drive for desktop and Google Photos stops working entirely. Any folders still configured for this kind of backup will no longer upload new photos or videos once the cutoff hits.Importantly, this doesn't mean Google Drive or Google Photos themselves are shutting down. Regular file syncing through the Drive desktop app will continue to work exactly as before — it's specifically the automatic bridge that pushed photos from a Drive-synced folder into Google Photos that's being removed. Google has also confirmed that any photos and videos already backed up to Google Photos through this method will remain safely stored and won't be affected by the change.For anyone who wants to keep automatic photo backups running, Google is directing users to set things up directly through Google Photos instead of via the Google Drive desktop app. There are two main options:* Continuous folder backup: In Google Photos, using the "+" button, users can select "Back up folders" and choose the computer folders they want backed up going forward, similar to how the Drive desktop app worked before.* Import from Drive: Users can also import photos that are already stored in their Google Drive folders directly into Google Photos.It is important to note that unlike the old Google Drive desktop integration, backups set up through the Google Photos website only run while the Google Photos site is open in a browser, rather than happening automatically in the background — a change that some users may find less convenient than the setup they are replacing.For casual users who mainly back up photos from their phones, this change will likely go unnoticed, since phone-based backups through the Google Photos app are not getting impacted. But for anyone who has used a computer folder — say, images imported from a camera or scanned documents — as their primary photo backup pipeline via the Google Drive desktop app, the deadline is worth acting on now. Missing it won't delete any existing backups, but it will quietly stop new photos from being backed up until the new setup is in place.
Article Summary: Google drive desktop app will stop supporting automatic google photos backup starting august 10, 2026. The change means that users who rely on drive’s desktop client to sync photos and videos from their computers will no longer see a new media automatically backed up to google photos.

Article Title: Anthropic has an important message for Claude users: Starting August 14, auto mode will be the default ...
Article Text:
How the Claude auto mode works

How to get started with the auto mode in Claude

Claude creator Boris Cherny is also the fan of this feature

What it means for users

Anthropic has announced that its auto mode will become the default setting for its Claude Code platform starting August 14. This change will affect the Pro, Max and Team accounts. With this new change in place, the developers will no longer need to manually approve each actin that AI takes during programming tasks. Instead, Claude Code will automatically process unless an action is deemed ‘irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your environment’. The company first introduced auto mode in March as a test feature designed to balance speed and control. In its latest announcement, Anthropic said testing showed auto mode to be safer than manual review — catching 89% of harmful actions compared to just 13.6% detected by human reviewers. The company noted that users tend to approve nearly all permission prompts manually, making automated oversight more effective.The company first introduced auto mode in March as a test feature designed to balance speed and control. In its latest announcement, Anthropic said testing showed auto mode to be safer than manual review — catching 89% of harmful actions compared to just 13.6% detected by human reviewers.The company noted that users tend to approve nearly all permission prompts manually, making automated oversight more effective.Claude doesn't reach for your mouse and keyboard right away. It first checks whether a connector exists for the job—Slack, Google Calendar, and a handful of other services are already wired in. If a connector handles it, that's the path it takes. Only when there's no direct integration does it fall back to controlling your screen.From there, it can open files, navigate a browser, type into forms, and click through menus—anything you'd do yourself. It always asks permission before touching a new application, and you can pull the plug at any point.The feature pairs with Dispatch, Anthropic's task-assignment tool that lets you delegate work from your phone. The combination is what makes the whole thing more than a novelty. Assign a task on your commute, and the finished output is waiting on your desktop when you sit down. You can also set recurring tasks—scan my inbox every morning, pull the weekly metrics every Friday—and Claude handles them on schedule without being asked again.The feature is available for Pro and Max subscribers. You need the Claude desktop app installed and running on macOS. The mobile app alone won't control your computer—but you can use it to assign tasks through Dispatch, which then execute on your desktop in the background.Claude Code Head Boris Cherny shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) that he and his team have been using auto mode exclusively for months, saying he “couldn’t imagine going back to permission prompts.” “The team and I use Auto mode exclusively, and have been for many months. I couldn't imagine going back to permission prompts! Really excited to get this out to everyone,” wrote Boris.Anthropic added that new safety features — including prompt injection screening and customizable hard deny rules — have been integrated to prevent data leaks and unauthorized actions.The update marks a significant step toward autonomous coding, reducing the need for human oversight while maintaining strong safety checks. For developers using Claude Code, the shift to auto mode is expected to streamline workflows and improve efficiency without compromising control.
Article Summary: Anthropic has announced that its auto mode will become the default setting for its claude code platform starting august 14. This change will affect the pro, max and team accounts. The company first introduced auto mode in march as a test feature designed to balance speed and control.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.
